api-errors.reason: ThalovantApiException in Errors.kt reads problem, errorCode and detail out of the error body once, exactly as sent, and apiError() in ControlPlane.kt builds one for every non-2xx response, reading the body as UTF-8; its bounded message now carries a string detail, with the bearer token and every string of 8 or more characters the request body sent redacted. Run against the shared API error vectors: each response is served by MockWebServer and read back through getHub(), and the message, toString() and stack trace are checked for every value the body echoed. 0.10.0: ControlPlane.kt gains browserLogin and interactiveLogin, which read errors through the same request() and apiError(); Errors.kt makes ThalovantApiException.errorCode settable internally (reading it is unchanged); re-run against the api-error vectors, results unchanged. Final reference 39e31d8: ControlPlane.kt's request() checks every URL against the API's origin, takes hidden values out of a failure's body before its message is built (none for this capability's calls, so its messages are unchanged), and can send a request at most once; these serve browser-login. Vector results unchanged.

binary.reason: HiveWire.decode branches on BINARY: four bits of payload type, then the clip itself, never parsed or inflated. onBinary() delivers it. Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than frames this SDK built for itself. A compressed part of a WIRE-1 frame inflates to at most 32 MiB (MAX_INFLATED); beyond that, or truncated, the frame is refused (ReviewFindingsTest).

browser-login.reason: ThalovantControlPlane.browserLogin(BrowserLoginOptions) and interactiveLogin(InteractiveLoginOptions) in ControlPlane.kt, ported to the final reference (39e31d8). The cleartext check runs before GET /v1/auth/native/config (no auth; a 404 keeps its status and problem, any other refusal is as is, and a 2xx NativeSignInConfig.fromJson refuses is a ThalovantApiException with no status). fromJson (NativeSignIn.kt) refuses a token_endpoint with a colon, a broken percent-escape, ?, #, \ or whitespace, and an authorization_endpoint on port 0 or above 65535 or whose host, as written, is not a bracketed IPv6 address, an IPv4 address (whenever the last label is numeric) or ASCII letter/digit/inner-hyphen labels of at most 253 characters. runBrowserLogin binds a LoopbackListener (Loopback.kt: a ServerSocket on InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1") port 0, reuseAddress off) before building the URL with NativeSignIn.browserAuthorizationUrl (RFC 3986 bytes, scope left out when empty, device_name cut to 120 code points; only a null name gets the default, an empty one is left out and the chooser's device login then sends no client_name); it prints or prompts the URL and opens the browser on a daemon thread (an injectable opener, else java.awt.Desktop, else open, xdg-open or rundll32; nothing on Android). classifyLoopbackRequest serves only GET /callback, answers a missing, repeated or wrong state 400 (MessageDigest.isEqual on UTF-8 bytes) and keeps waiting, decodes once as parse_qsl does, lets an error win over a code and keeps only RFC 6749's seven error codes; a HEAD gets the headers and no body; the first accepted callback closes the port and its tab waits until the sign-in ends (no deadline of its own; closing answers it); every answer carries the five page headers and is followed by shutting the write side and draining for at most 2 s and 1 MiB. Denied is ThalovantDeviceLoginDeniedException and the monotonic timeout ThalovantDeviceLoginExpiredException, both with no status; a consent-page error is a status-less ThalovantApiException whose errorCode (internally settable in Errors.kt) is that code or null. The exchange POSTs exactly code, code_verifier, client_id and redirect_uri through request(), which refuses any URL off the API's origin (sameOrigin), redacts the code, the verifier and the state from the answer before the message is built (scrubSecrets/scrubBody in BrowserLogin.kt: one pass, longest first, never inside [redacted]) and sends it at most once (retryOnConnectionFailure off, a one-shot body, so OkHttp replays it neither after a connection failure nor on a 408 or a 503 Retry-After: 0); withoutSecrets always builds a new error with no cause, and a transport failure is a new IOException. The token is kept through acceptToken, as a device login does, so revokeApiToken revokes it idempotently. The chooser uses NativeSignIn.canOpenBrowser (CI, SSH_CONNECTION, SSH_TTY; macos and windows; else DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY), asks for the configuration only then, falls back to a device login on any ThalovantApiException or IOException before the browser is opened, never after, and runs its opener on a daemon thread on both paths. Device login and NativeSignIn.begin/completeNativeSignIn are unchanged. BrowserLoginVectorsTest runs all 119 shared browser-login vectors: the pure sections against the functions that decide them (the callbacks through a real listener too), sign_ins and chooser for real over OkHttp against a MockWebServer that serves each case's exchanges in order and checks every request, with a raw socket playing the browser; results recorded in contracts/conformance-results.json and matching the reference case for case, the 98 earlier cases unchanged. BrowserLoginTest covers what the vectors do not: the prints and opener threads, idle, oversized and early-closing connections, the tab's wait, HEAD, the drain and its bound, cancellation, redaction across the message cut, at-most-once delivery of the exchange, the origin check, cleartext, and the endpoint rules.

connection-admission.reason: ThalovantControlPlane.waitForAdmission(result | operation) polls GET /v1/operations/{id}, every read bounded by what is left of the wait: ready, no operation and 404 are admitted; a 5xx is ridden out; a 429 waits max(poll interval, ThalovantApiException.retryAfterSeconds -- the body's retry_after_seconds at the top or inside its detail object, else Retry-After, else RateLimit-Reset) and is a timeout at once when that is more than is left; 401 and 403 are thrown as the API's own ThalovantAuthException (and its kin); failed and timed_out, and any other refusal of the wait, throw ThalovantAdmissionFailedException, the operation's errorCode for the first and the API's statusCode, code, detail and problem for the second; an API out of reach throws the IOException it is. The deadline throws ThalovantAdmissionTimeoutException, whose message ends "it may still admit it later", which extends ThalovantConnectionException and implements the ThalovantTimeout interface ThalovantTimeoutException also implements. A links.self whose origin -- scheme, host and port, the default port spelled out -- is not the API's is refused before any request. Run against the shared admission vectors over OkHttp and MockWebServer, with the scripted response headers, {api_host}/{api_port} filled in and a closed loopback port for the unreachable API; results recorded and matching the reference. 0.10.0: ControlPlane.kt and Errors.kt change for browser-login only; HomeLinkControlPlaneTest's revoke-race test now gates the sign-in's answer on the DELETE (it was flaky); re-run against the admission vectors, results unchanged. Final reference 39e31d8: ControlPlane.kt's request() checks every URL against the API's origin, takes hidden values out of a failure's body before its message is built (none for this capability's calls, so its messages are unchanged), and can send a request at most once; these serve browser-login. Vector results unchanged.

Run against the shared connection-kinds vectors over OkHttp and MockWebServer, recording the requests sent in order; results recorded and matching the reference. 0.10.0: ControlPlane.kt and Errors.kt change for browser-login only; HomeLinkControlPlaneTest's revoke-race test now gates the sign-in's answer on the DELETE (it was flaky); re-run against the connection-kinds vectors, results unchanged. Vector results unchanged.

control.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. The authorization-code grant with PKCE is covered here alongside the device grant: the challenge is checked to be S256 of the verifier, the verifier never to reach the browser, a redirect answering a different attempt or carrying error= to be refused, and the token exchange to refuse cleartext to a non-loopback host. 0.10.0: NativeSignIn gains the browser sign-in pieces (browserAuthorizationUrl, loopbackRedirectUri, newState, canOpenBrowser, defaultDeviceName, NativeSignInConfig) and ControlPlane.kt browserLogin and interactiveLogin; NativeSignIn.begin, codeFrom and completeNativeSignIn are unchanged and NativeSignInTest still passes. Final reference 39e31d8: NativeSignIn's browser sign-in rules tighten (token_endpoint colon and escapes, authorization_endpoint port 0 and host); NativeSignIn.begin, codeFrom and completeNativeSignIn are unchanged and NativeSignInTest still passes.

device-login.reason: ThalovantControlPlane.beginDeviceLogin, pollDeviceLogin and revokeApiToken in ControlPlane.kt (an empty scope list is left out of the request, in loginWithBrowser too), with DeviceAuthorization and ApiToken; ThalovantDeviceLoginPendingException (a ThalovantApiException carrying intervalMillis) in Errors.kt, and the denied and expired exceptions, which keep their ThalovantException supertype and now carry statusCode and body. slow_down lengthens a device code's interval by five seconds for good; an approved poll stores accessToken and tokenId, and every sign-in (login, completeNativeSignIn, the device flow) sets tokenId from its own answer or clears it; revoking the token in use is idempotent -- a 401 there counts as revoked, and a second revoke sends nothing -- while another token's refusal is thrown; loginWithBrowser runs on the same steps. Run against the shared device-login vectors over OkHttp: each case's exchanges are served in order by MockWebServer, every request is checked (method, path, body, Authorization), and the message, toString and stack trace of every error are checked for the device code and the token. The results are recorded in contracts/conformance-results.json and match the reference's. 0.9.1: beginDeviceLogin and DeviceLoginOptions take clientId (HOME_ASSISTANT_CLIENT_ID), sent as client_id only when given, with the 0.8.0 JVM signatures kept as hidden overloads; describeDeviceLogin(userCode) reads GET /v1/auth/device/codes/{user_code} into DeviceLoginRequest, verified only with a client_id; every device-token POST is bounded by what is left of the sign-in. 0.10.0: loginWithBrowser delegates to a private deviceLogin with the same steps, so interactiveLogin can pass its opener to the verification page; behaviour unchanged. HomeLinkControlPlaneTest's revoke-race test holds the sign-in's answer until the DELETE arrives, so the revoke always reads its target first (it failed on a loaded machine when the sign-in finished before the revoke began) and still fails against an unconditional forget. Re-run against the device-login vectors, results unchanged. Final reference 39e31d8: ControlPlane.kt's request() checks every URL against the API's origin, takes hidden values out of a failure's body before its message is built (none for this capability's calls, so its messages are unchanged), and can send a request at most once; these serve browser-login. Vector results unchanged.

home-link.reason: replyContext() in Events.kt and ThalovantClient.reply build the OVOS-MSG-1 5.2 reply from the context exactly as the hub sent it (this SDK delivers the raw context); a destination with no source gives a reply with no destination. Home.kt holds the contract (ThalovantHome), HomeRequest, HomeAnswer, homeResponse, plainSpeech (only real tags, comments and processing instructions removed, in linear time, by the reference's one-pass tag rule; numeric references, the five XML entities and   decoded; Unicode White_Space collapsed) and answerHomeRequest(s) on a client or a HubSession: the handler runs detached with its timeout or what is left of the hub's 10 s from arrival, the answer goes out at the deadline even when the handler ignores cancellation, and the reply's sending is bounded by what the handler left and withdrawn after it. Keeping the link: closeRefuses() in Transport.kt reads 1000, 1005 and 1008 during the handshake or within 750 ms after it as a refusal; a hub answer that does not authenticate is a refusal; a failed KK attempt is followed at once by one XX attempt inside the same connect, and a hub key that is not the pinned one is ThalovantHubIdentityChangedException, checked before this side answers; an upgrade answered 401 or 403 is a refusal. LinkSupervisor in Session.kt holds the retry ladder, the immediate redial after a drop, the 600 s refusal grace and the immediate stop on a changed key, and HubSession.run follows it; HubSession.reply never waits behind a running ask. The home-link cases run through ThalovantClient.answerHomeRequest and its reply path; LinkKeepingVectorsTest runs close cases through closeRefuses, handshake cases through the real WSS transport against FakeHub (an in-process Noise hub with KK, XX, password and key changes and upgrade statuses, recording the patterns chosen) and supervise cases through LinkSupervisor. Results recorded and matching the reference. 0.9.1: any frame that decrypts after the handshake -- JSON, WIRE-1 binary, a chunk, the hub's HELLO -- makes a later refusal-code close a drop (closeRefuses afterAuthenticatedFrame); a refused close as an XX handshake ends is ThalovantClientKeyRejectedException, a ThalovantIdentityException naming the key folders, on which LinkSupervisor (after(..., clientKeyRejected = true), carried beside LinkOutcome.REFUSED rather than as a new enum entry) and HubSession.run give up at once; a reply that went out records the link as up, and so does every link HubSession makes, whichever call made it.

identity.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. An identity read from a file (ThalovantIdentity.sourcePath) keeps its Noise key in HiveMindNoiseStore.forIdentity's folder beside that file, copying -- never moving -- the key and pins this SDK kept in the shared default when that key has met the hub (ReviewFindingsTest). 0.9.5 reference: endpointFor(WSS) reads a wss:// or ws:// default_master in any case when no WSS endpoint is named (it was lowercase-only); an explicit endpoint wins, an http(s) master gives none, the master is never MQTT (IdentityTest).

intercom.reason: The Android SDK is the app's data plane to its hubs. Intercom announcements (an announce-only text spoken aloud on a household hub's speakers, POST /v1/hubs/{hub_id}/intercom/announce) are sent from the console, the Python, Node, Go and Rust SDKs or the MCP server, which the intercom contract (section F) names as the only consumers; this SDK only ever receives speech as an ordinary client. A port is a separate decision to record in the API's impact file first, not a silent gap.

refusal.reason: failureError() and refusalBelongsToAsk() in Errors.kt, used by ask() in Client.kt, which counts asks, queries and fire-and-forget utterances inside the shared grace window -- recorded once connected and immediately before the publish, and kept when the publish throws. Run against the shared refusal vectors; TransportTest drives denials over the real transport and RuntimeTest covers an ask beside a query and beside a fire-and-forget send. 0.10.0: Errors.kt makes ThalovantApiException.errorCode settable internally for browser-login; failureError and refusalBelongsToAsk are unchanged; re-run against the refusal vectors, results unchanged.

runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs. A skill may now positively assert a genuine claim from the fallback tier via a literal `true` under `THALOVANT_CLAIMED_META_KEY` (`thalovant_claimed`) in its own `speak` event's `meta` object; `ThalovantReply.claimed` checks it after the handled/ok/no-failure gate, so it can only ever turn a would-be false into true, and a reply that never sets it is judged exactly as before. The scan is restricted to that speak event alone (`ThalovantEvents.SPEAK`/`OVOS_UTTERANCE_SPEAK`), never any other correlated event the reply collected, so a correlated `ovos.utterance.handled` carrying the same meta shape cannot assert a claim (0.9.2).

session.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. The connected-client factory owns failed connection cleanup; Python performs that dial internally and retains failed retirement before replacement. HubSession.run keeps the link by the same policy as the reference's AsyncHubSession.run, and reply never waits behind a running ask (HomeLinkSessionTest).
